newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels say ready to talk with gov't - radio.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels say ready to talk with gov't - radio.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist rebels holding 73 hostages in Lima said on Saturday they were ready to start face-to-face talks with the government to reach a negotiated solution to the month-old crisis, local radio said.

But the rebels added that talks would achieve nothing if the government persisted in ruling out their principal demand for the release of jailed comrades, according to a communique from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) read to local Radio Programas del Peru via two-way radio.

In the communique, a rebel spokesman assumed to be MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, speaking from within the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence, accepted the government's proposal of a Canadian government representative on a "guarantor" committee overseeing the talks.

"The government proposal to include a representative from Canada is acceptable, I repeat, is acceptable," the spokesman said in the communique which was played by Radio Programas. Government negotiator Domingo Palermo said on Friday former hostage and Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent would sit on the commission. Palermo also proposed meeting outside the residence.

"About the place of the meeting, we take note of the proposal and through internal channels we will respond. Through those means we will also specify better the role of the guarantors, because we believe all serious and responsible negotiation cannot be only through public communiques," said the rebel spokesman.
Within a framework of discussing all issues, including the demand to free jailed MRTA members, "we are ready to converse as we were willing to since we occupied this diplomatic site," he added.
